subject: Cognitive Science
title: Goal-Derived Categories
description: A short lesson to help you apply Goal-Derived Categories.

hook.text: "Things to grab if the house is on fire." That's a real category, but no textbook lists it.

buildup.text: Ad hoc categories are created on the fly to serve a goal, not stored in long-term memory.

discovery.text: Lawrence Barsalou showed that these categories have graded structure just like natural ones.

twist.text: Passport is more typical of "things to save in a fire" than piano. Typicality tracks usefulness.

climax.text: This proves categorization is flexible—the mind builds new groups whenever goals demand it.

punchline.text: Need invents categories on the spot.
